Article Title: Asian Games Medal Tally: India win 8 medals but remain outside top 10 as gold continues to elude
Article Text:
Yashvir Singh, Rohit Yadav, and Esha Singh

Eight medals, but no gold for India

Shooting and kurash add to India's tally

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage claimed gold with 88.55m.Sreeshankar also won silver in the men's long jump with 8.07m despite an injury forcing him to abandon his final two attempts. China's Yuhao Shi took gold with 8.17m.Gulveer added his second silver of the Games with a personal best of 3:36.72 in the men's 1500m, having earlier finished runner-up in the 10,000m.Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5000m with 15:14.61, adding to the bronze she had claimed in the 3000m steeplechase.Vithya Ramraj also took bronze in the women's 400m hurdles with a personal best of 54.75 seconds.Esha Singh secured silver in the women's 25m pistol after finishing with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won the gold after the shoot-off.Pincky Balhara added bronze in the women's -78kg kurash category, losing 0-5 to South Korea's Sumin Mo in the semifinals.Despite the eight medals, India's gold tally remained at four, a crucial factor in the standings as countries are ranked by gold medals first.China led with 132 golds, followed by Japan with 41, South Korea with 21 and Uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.
Article Summary: India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. China led with 132 golds, followed by japan with 41, south korea with 21 and uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.

Article Title: ‘This is not cricket’: Gautam Gambhir questions Guwahati pitch after India chase 406 with ease
Article Text:
India's coach Gautam Gambhir, left, chats with captain Shubman Gill during a practice session. (AP Photo)

‘It’s not fair for the bowlers’

Gambhir backs exposure for young bowlers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir had little doubt about the entertainment value of Wednesday’s extraordinary run-fest in Guwahati, but he was far less impressed by the conditions that allowed both teams to score more than 400 runs.After West Indies posted 405 for seven, India chased down the target in just 43.3 overs, winning by eight wickets to seal the three-match ODI series 2-0. Shubman Gill smashed an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls, while Rohit Sharma scored 101 off 75 as India completed the highest successful run chase in their ODI history.Yet, for Gambhir, the remarkable numbers also highlighted a concern. He felt the pitch offered too little to the bowlers and called for a greater balance between bat and ball.“Look, if I have to be absolutely honest, I feel I think there has to be a bit of more contest between bat and ball, because I think you talk about cricket - but this is not cricket, this is only batting,” Gambhir told Star Sports after the match.“Because imagine a young bowler bowling on this wicket, and the opposition getting 400 and then we go on to chase 400. Obviously, for the records it's outstanding, for the crowd it's outstanding, for the broadcaster it's outstanding, but if you ask me as a genuine cricket fan and as a coach, because I have to have sympathy for the bowlers as well.”“When you bowl on this kind of a wicket, it's not fair for the bowlers. So we've got to give something to the bowlers so there's at least something which the bowlers can work with,” he added.The Guwahati surface produced a stunning batting display, with West Indies reaching 405 for seven before India responded with 406 for two.John Campbell, Shai Hope and Amir Jangoo struck centuries for West Indies, while Gill and Rohit then led the Indian chase. Gill's unbeaten 223 was the defining innings of the day, while his opening partnership of 255 with Rohit was India's second-highest in men's ODIs. Virat Kohli , who had scored a century in the first ODI, contributed 29 off 19 balls before falling, while Ruturaj Gaikwad made 31 off 37.The match became only the second successful chase of a target of 400 or more in men's ODI history, after South Africa's famous 438-run chase against Australia in 2006.For Gambhir, however, the scale of the scoring made it important to consider what the conditions meant for the bowlers rather than simply celebrating the batting numbers.“The first thing is that you need some sympathy and a bit of margin for the bowlers,” he said.“Often you can't be hard on bowlers, because sometimes bowling figures are such that they haven't bowled as poorly as their figures suggest. Because the margin is very small.”He also pointed to the restrictions modern-day bowlers face in ODI cricket, including fielding restrictions, two new balls and the increasing power of batters.“Plus, I think you can only bowl in good areas because besides that, with five fielders inside, two new balls, and the kind of power-hitting there is now, bowlers don't really have many options,” Gambhir said.“That is why, as a coach, as a support staff, the first thing you look at is, were they able to execute their bowling or their plans properly? If they were able to do that, then you shouldn't be hard on them.”“If you get too hard just looking at their analysis, then we will never be able to develop bowlers.”India gave Auqib Nabi his ODI debut despite already leading the series 1-0, and Gambhir said putting inexperienced bowlers into difficult situations was an important part of India's preparation for the 2027 ODI World Cup.“Imagine Auqib [Nabi] playing his first game... somewhere you need to give them a bit of support and keep a bit of an extra cushion or extra options for them,” he said. “But unfortunately, today there wasn't much for any bowler.”Gambhir said India could have waited until the third ODI, when the series would already be decided, to give Nabi an opportunity. But he argued that a dead rubber would not recreate the pressure young players could experience at a World Cup.“We could have given Auqib a chance in the next match too when it's a dead rubber, but in a dead rubber, you don't have that pressure which comes with the pressure of winning a series,” he said.“And we all know that the World Cup is all about pressure. Cricket isn't going to change like that, only the pressure will be different because the World Cup comes once in four years, so we want to put bowlers under pressure.”He also cited Gurnoor Brar as an example of a young bowler who could benefit from being exposed to demanding phases of an ODI.“For example, Gurnoor [Brar]. Having Gurnoor bowl in the first 10 overs, bowling at the death, I know people will talk about his analysis, but the more he bowls in tough conditions, in tough situations, the better it is for Indian cricket,” Gambhir said.“Because you can have him bowl in the middle overs and get good analysis or good stats for him, make him bowl defensively, but the more we expose them at such times, the better it is for Indian cricket.”
Article Summary: India coach gautam gambhir says the pitch offered too little to the bowlers. India beat west indies by eight wickets to win three-match odi series 2-0. Shubman gill smashed an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls as india completed the highest successful run chase in their odi history.

Article Title: Brij Bhushan acquittal challenged over ‘stereotypical assumptions’ about sexual assault victims
Article Text:
Wrestlers challenge acquittal, cite ‘stereotypical assumptions’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Rouse Avenue court has issued notice to former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and others on an appeal challenging his acquittal in a sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers.Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh sought a response to the appeal and listed the matter for hearing on October 9. The court also directed that the original affidavit and orders containing the names of the victims be placed in a sealed envelope. It further directed the appellant to file a copy of the petition with the victims’ names redacted.The appeal challenges the August 3 order of the Rouse Avenue court, Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar in the case. The wrestlers have contended that the acquittal order is unsustainable in law and is based on a “manifestly erroneous and selective appreciation of the evidence on record”.The appeal has contended that the impugned order proceeds on conjectures and surmises, fails to apply binding and well-settled principles of law, and, in material part, rests its reasoning on “archaic and stereotypical assumptions” about the “expected” behaviour of victims of sexual assault and harassment, rather than on a fair, evidence-based assessment after taking into account the circumstances of the victims.The case stems from an FIR filed by Delhi Police following a complaint by a woman wrestler during Singh’s tenure as WFI chief. The police had invoked Sections 354, 354-D, 354-A, 506(1) and 109 of the Indian Penal Code.Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwani Panwar had acquitted Singh and Tomar after a trial that was conducted in a closed courtroom. The two were tried in connection with allegations of sexual harassment of women wrestlers in India and abroad.Delhi Police had filed a 1,500-page charge sheet against Singh and Tomar on June 15, 2023, following its investigation into the allegations.The women wrestlers had earlier staged a protest at Jantar Mantar, following which the FIR was registered by Delhi Police based on the complaint.Advocate Rajiv Mohan, assisted by Rehan Khan and Rishabh Bhati, represented Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, while senior advocate Rebecca John appeared for the victims and complainants.
Article Summary: Wrestlers challenge acquittal, cite ‘stereotypical assumptions’ special judge dig vinay singh sought a response to the appeal and listed the matter for hearing on october 9. The appeal challenges the august 3 order of the rouse avenue court, brij bhushan and vinod tomar in the case.

Article Title: India crush Sri Lanka by 124 runs, set up Asian Games gold-medal clash against Pakistan
Article Text:
India's Jasprit Bumrah celebrates with teammates after taking the wicket of Sri Lanka's Sineth Jayawardena. (PTI Photo)

Bumrah, Axar set up Sri Lanka collapse

Kishan, Sooryavanshi rescue India

Pakistan await in gold-medal clash

NEW DELHI: India produced a dominant all-round performance to crush Sri Lanka by 124 runs in the second men's cricket semifinal of the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Thursday, setting up a mouth-watering gold-medal clash against arch-rivals Pakistan on Saturday.After posting 169/7 on a turning pitch, India tore through Sri Lanka's batting line-up with a devastating new-ball burst and bowled them out for just 45 in 9.5 overs. The defending champions' bowlers never allowed Sri Lanka to settle into the chase, with Jasprit Bumrah, Axar Patel and Abhishek Sharma leading the rout.Pakistan had earlier booked their place in the final after beating Bangladesh by six wickets in the rain-truncated first semifinal.Defending 170, India made an explosive start as Bumrah struck twice in his opening over. A run-out in the second over added to Sri Lanka's problems, leaving them three wickets down almost immediately.Axar then tightened the screws in the fourth over, picking up two wickets to reduce Sri Lanka to 18/5. With the pitch offering considerable assistance to the spinners, the chase quickly turned into a procession.Sri Lanka continued to lose wickets at regular intervals and had no answer to India's disciplined attack. Abhishek eventually completed the demolition job, taking two wickets in two balls to wrap up the innings at 45.The margin of victory underlined India's complete control of the semifinal and ensured the defending champions moved into Saturday's gold-medal match without having to face a serious challenge after the powerplay.India had also been tested with the bat after Sri Lanka opted to bowl first. The turning conditions made stroke-making difficult, and Sri Lanka used spin almost exclusively during the early part of the innings.Abhishek Sharma fell for seven after hitting a six, while Sanju Samson was dismissed for seven by ambidextrous spinner Tharindu Ratnayake.Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, however, provided the spark India needed. The 15-year-old smashed 38 from just 21 balls, peppering the Sri Lankan attack with trademark strokeplay before falling to Sahan Arachchige.His innings included six fours and two sixes and helped India reach 58/2 in the powerplay. But wickets continued to fall, with captain Shreyas Iyer and Axar Patel also departing as Sri Lanka's spinners kept the pressure on.It was left to Ishan Kishan to provide the finishing push. The left-hander remained unbeaten on 80 from 46 balls, attacking the spinners down the ground and finding the boundary regularly. Four of his sixes came between long-on and long-off, while he also struck four fours.Kishan's composed assault ensured India reached a competitive 169/7, a total that proved more than enough once Bumrah and the spinners got to work.India's reward for the comprehensive victory is a high-profile final against Pakistan on Saturday. The two sides will now meet with the Asian Games gold medal at stake, adding another chapter to their long-running sporting rivalry.For India, the semifinal offered a reminder of their depth across both departments. Kishan and Sooryavanshi provided the impetus with the bat, while Bumrah's early strikes and Axar's double blow ensured Sri Lanka's chase never got going.The focus now shifts to the final, where India will look to complete their campaign with gold against Pakistan.
Article Summary: India crush sri lanka by 124 runs in asian games men's cricket semifinal. Jasprit bumrah, axar patel and abhishek sharma lead rout of sri lanka. India will face arch-rivals pakistan in saturday's gold-medal match.

Article Title: India-Pakistan rivalry takes centre stage as hockey heavyweights meet in Asian Games semifinal
Article Text:
Kakamigahara, Sep 30 (IANS) Another chapter in one of international hockey’s most storied rivalries will unfold on Thursday when defending champions India face Pakistan in the first semifinal of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026, with a place in the gold-medal match on the line.

Pal ruled out

Irrespective of the widening gap in recent results, India-Pakistan hockey has never been just another match. The rivalry carries an emotion few other contests can match, and it will take centre stage again when the cross-border rivals meet in the Asian Games men’s semifinal.India have been unbeaten in the tournament, winning all five of their league fixtures. Their toughest test came against hosts Japan, whom they beat 2-0.Pakistan, meanwhile, were expected to top their pool but a narrow 4-5 defeat to Malaysia pushed them into second place and brought the old rivals together in the semifinal. It also ended the possibility of an India-Pakistan gold-medal clash.On paper, India — unbeaten against Pakistan for a decade — will start with the better recent record. But with an Olympic berth at stake, there is little room for complacency.The defending champions have been prolific in front of goal, scoring 49 times. Striker Dilpreet Singh leads the charts with nine, while Harmanpreet and Abhishek have eight each. Fifteen of India’s goals have come from penalty corners.Pakistan, however, have a potent weapon of their own. Drag-flicker Sufiyan Khan has been in excellent touch, scoring 11 goals in the league phase.India will be without midfielder Raj Kumar Pal, who has been ruled out after fracturing his left thumb during the final league match against Bangladesh. Travelling reserve Nilakanta Sharma will take his place in the squad.India’s dominance in the classic rivalry is reflected in their last Asian Games meeting, when they thrashed Pakistan 10-2 in the league phase in 2023. However, in the recent FIH World Cup, India were made to sweat for a 5-3 victory.Dwelling on the last-four contest, Harmanpreet said, “Pakistan is always a special challenge, and we know a semifinal demands our complete focus. We have worked hard throughout this tournament and built good momentum. In the semifinals, it is about staying calm, trusting our preparation, playing together and giving everything for India. We want to earn our place in the final.”In the other semifinal, Malaysia take on South Korea.
Article Summary: Defending champions india face pakistan in the first semifinal of the aichi-nagoya asian games 2026. India have been unbeaten in the tournament, winning all five of their league fixtures. Pakistan, meanwhile, were expected to top their pool but a narrow 4-5 defeat to malaysia pushed them into second place.

Article Title: Josh Hokit again stirs controversy, accuses Alex Pereira of witchcraft and claims ‘Chama’ is a curse ahead of UFC 334 fight
Article Text:
Josh Hokit (Image via IG/X)

Josh Hokit claims Alex Pereira’s ‘Chama’ puts curses on people

Josh Hokit has taken another bizarre shot at Alex Pereira, accusing the former UFC light heavyweight champion of witchcraft and claiming his famous “Chama” catchphrase is connected to curses. Hokit made the comments while discussing Pereira’s push for the heavyweight title opportunity during an appearance on Beyond You Me Podcast. He previously made the same claims during The Ariel Helwani Show.Hokit said Pereira’s face paint, “Chama” slogan and indigenous background were linked to supernatural practices. He also claimed the entire world had unknowingly been chanting Pereira’s supposed curse.Josh Hokit’s comments came while the undefeated heavyweight was discussing his upcoming undisputed title fight with Ciryl Gane. Pereira had also been campaigning for the same opportunity, giving Hokit another reason to take aim at the Brazilian star.Instead of focusing only on the heavyweight title picture, Hokit turned his attention toward Pereira’s appearance, catchphrase and cultural background.He said, “The aura-less sorceress is what I call him. The b*tch that be doing witchcraft - and we finally caught on to it. He’s had the whole world chanting ‘Chama,’ putting curses on the whole world.”Hokit also discussed Pereira’s face paint and the meaning he associates with the fighter’s famous “Chama” phrase.“Alex Pereira. He paints his face in women’s mascara. He’s witchcraft. He wants to say Chama, and that sh**t is from, you know, the shaman. And shamans, they don’t believe in the one true God”, he added.He went even further by suggesting Pereira’s alleged practices were responsible for his recent defeat against Gane.“So it’s like everyone’s saying Chama, and it’s like it’s putting curses on everybody. You know what I’m saying? That’s why he got f**ked up by Ciryl Gane. The wrath of God came upon him”, he said.Pereira’s indigenous heritage has been part of his public identity. The Brazilian fighter has Pataxo ancestry and has participated in traditional Pataxo dances, blessings and cleansing rituals. Hokit, however, presented his own interpretation of those practices while making the witchcraft accusations.The comments are also not the first time Pereira has faced supernatural claims from another fighter. Former UFC light heavyweight champion Jiří Procházka previously accused Pereira of using shamanistic magic to gain an advantage in his fights.For Hokit, the focus now shifts to his own heavyweight title challenge. He is scheduled to face Gane for the undisputed heavyweight championship on November 14 at Madison Square Garden at UFC 334.Hokit enters the contest undefeated. He has already recorded two victories in 2026. He defeated Curtis Blaydes by unanimous decision in April before stopping Derrick Lewis with a second-round TKO at UFC Freedom 250 in June.The American has also promised an intense fight against Gane. Hokit has outlined his approach and predicted a difficult night for the French heavyweight.
Article Summary: Josh hokit claims alex pereira’s ‘chama’ puts curses on people. Former ufc light heavyweight champion made the comments during an appearance on beyond you me podcast. Hokit is scheduled to face ciryl gane for the undisputed heavyweight championship on november 14 at madison square garden.

Article Title: 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi named among rising stars alongside Arch Manning, Tyrese Maxey, Olivia Miles
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Arch Manning and Tyrese Maxey. (Image credit: Agencies)

From IPL auction to international cricket

Youngest List A centurion

Fastest List A fifty

More records in T20 cricket

Making his mark in international cricket

NEW DELHI: Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has added another major achievement to his growing list of records. The young Indian batter has been named on TIME100 Next 2026, a list of 100 rising stars whom TIME has identified as people who could shape the future of their respective fields.Sooryavanshi is the youngest person on this year's list and one of seven athletes to feature.The other athletes include American football quarterback Arch Manning, NBA star Tyrese Maxey, footballers Naomi Girma and Folarin Balogun, tennis player Alexandra Eala and basketball player Olivia Miles.Sooryavanshi first made headlines when Rajasthan Royals signed him at the IPL auction in 2024. At 13, he became the youngest player ever bought at an IPL auction.He made his IPL debut in 2025 and soon created history by becoming the youngest player to score a century in men's T20 cricket. He smashed a 35-ball century for Rajasthan Royals against Gujarat Titans in IPL 2025 after reaching his half-century in just 17 balls.His performances have continued to break records across formats.Sooryavanshi became the youngest player to score a century in men's List A cricket when he hit 190 off 84 balls for Bihar against Arunachal Pradesh in the 2025-26 Vijay Hazare Trophy.He reached his century in only 36 balls and got to 150 in 59 balls, setting another record for the fastest 150 in men's List A cricket. His century came at the age of 14 years and 272 days, breaking the previous record held by Zahoor Elahi.Sooryavanshi also holds the record for the fastest fifty in men's List A cricket. He reached the landmark in just 11 balls while playing for India A against Sri Lanka A in June 2026.He eventually scored 94 off 29 balls in the tri-series final.The teenager has also made his mark in T20 cricket.Sooryavanshi became the fastest player to hit 100 sixes in T20 cricket, reaching the mark in just 514 balls and 29 innings.In IPL 2026, he scored 776 runs and hit 72 sixes. He also became the fastest player to reach 1,000 IPL runs, getting there in 440 balls. He crossed 1,000 runs in T20 cricket in 473 balls, another record.Sooryavanshi made his international debut on India's tour of the UK in 2026.After a difficult start, he bounced back on the tour of Zimbabwe and smashed an 18-ball half-century, becoming the youngest player to score a fifty in men's international cricket. He was also named Player of the Series after scoring 151 runs at a strike rate of 196.10 in India's 3-0 T20I series win over Zimbabwe.At 15 years and 121 days, he became the youngest male player to win a Player-of-the-Series award in international cricket.
Article Summary: Vaibhav sooryavanshi has been named on time100 next 2026. He is the youngest person on this year's list and one of seven athletes to feature. The other athletes include american football quarterback arch manning, nba star tyrese maxey and tennis player alexandra eala.

NEW DELHI: India added another medal to their Asian Games 2026 tally on Thursday as Ganesh Mani Ratnam Thirumuru secured bronze in the men’s individual compound archery event at Aichi-Nagoya.Ganesh produced a dominant performance in the bronze-medal match, defeating Vietnam’s Cong Duc Dang 149-144. The Indian archer was almost flawless, hitting 10s with 14 of his 15 arrows to comfortably seal the podium finish.The bronze took India’s overall medal tally to 63, comprising 10 gold, 22 silver and 31 bronze.Ganesh made an ideal start to the bronze-medal match, opening with a perfect 10 while Cong managed an 8. The Vietnamese archer responded with two 10s, but Ganesh matched him with two more perfect shots to maintain his advantage.The Indian completed the opening end with a perfect 30/30, while Cong finished on 29, giving Ganesh a one-point lead.He continued to maintain his accuracy through the remaining ends, with his consistent shooting eventually giving him a five-point winning margin.Ganesh's 149 was enough to comfortably see off Cong, who finished on 144, and secure India's fourth medal in compound archery at the Games.Ganesh's bronze came a day after India enjoyed a hugely successful outing in the compound events, winning three gold medals on Wednesday.His medal also ensured India added another bronze to their growing tally, taking the country's haul to 63 medals.Ganesh had earlier narrowly missed out on a place in the gold-medal contest after losing his semifinal 144-148 to Kim Jongho of South Korea. The Indian began the final end with consecutive 9s, but the deficit proved too difficult to overturn as Kim held on to advance to the final.Ganesh bounced back strongly in the bronze-medal match, delivering a near-perfect performance to finish on the podium.The focus in archery now shifts to the recurve events, which begin on Friday, giving India's archers another opportunity to add to the country's medal tally at Aichi-Nagoya.

Article Title: Shubman Gill scripts history, becomes first captain to score double centuries in Test and ODIs
Article Text:
Shubman Gill scripts cricket history

From Edgbaston 269 to Guwahati 223*

Fastest double century in ODI history

Shubman Gill did not just produce another breathtaking innings on Wednesday night. He created a record that had never been achieved in international cricket before.The Indian captain smashed an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls against West Indies in the second ODI in Guwahati, becoming the first captain to score a double century in both Test and ODI cricket. Gill had previously scored 269 against England at Edgbaston in 2025, making his latest feat a unique chapter in the history of captaincy.What made the Guwahati innings even more remarkable was the situation. West Indies had posted 405/7, their first-ever 400-plus ODI total, after centuries from John Campbell, Shai Hope and Amir Jangoo. India then chased down 406 in just 43.3 overs, winning by eight wickets with 39 balls to spare.Gill's latest record cannot be viewed in isolation. In July 2025, while leading India in the Test series against England, he produced historic innings at Edgbaston. His 269 off 387 balls became the highest score by an Indian captain in Test cricket and the highest score by an Indian captain in a Test in England.That innings already placed Gill in an exclusive group of captains to score Test double centuries in England.Now, with his Guwahati double century, he has added an unprecedented ODI achievement to that record. Gill became the first captain to score a double century in both Test and ODI cricket.Gill reached his double century in just 117 balls, breaking Ishan Kishan's previous record of 126 balls. His 223* also became the highest individual score in a successful ODI chase, surpassing Glenn Maxwell's unbeaten 201 against Afghanistan.By the time he reached 223, Gill had hit 26 fours and eight sixes, finishing with the highest ODI score of his career. His previous best was the 208 he scored against New Zealand in Hyderabad in 2023.That makes Gill only the second Indian after Rohit Sharma to score multiple ODI double centuries. Rohit remains the only batter with three ODI double tons.Gill's individual brilliance came during a chase that itself entered the record books. India's 406/2 became their highest successful ODI chase, surpassing their previous record. It was also only the second time a team had successfully chased a target of 400 or more in men's ODI cricket, after South Africa's famous 438-run chase against Australia in Johannesburg in 2006.The foundation was laid by Gill and Rohit Sharma, who put together a remarkable 255-run opening partnership. Rohit contributed 101 before being dismissed, leaving Gill to complete the chase alongside Ruturaj Gaikwad.The match therefore produced an unusual statistical symmetry: West Indies made 405, three of their batters scored centuries, and India chased the target with two centuries of their own.The Guwahati double century also took Gill to his 11th ODI century in just 68 innings. He became the fastest Indian to reach 11 ODI hundreds, moving ahead of Virat Kohli's mark of 82 innings. Hashim Amla remains the fastest overall, having reached the milestone in 64 innings.
Article Summary: Shubman gill becomes the first captain to score a double century in both test and odi cricket. The indian captain smashed an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls against west indies in the second odi in guwahati. Gill had previously scored 269 against england at edgbaston in 2025, making his latest feat a unique chapter in the history of captaincy.

Article Title: A 500-year-old football was found in a queen’s bedroom; in 2026, scientists scanned it so the object could live digitally
Article Text:
The ball was found behind panelling in the Queen’s Chamber at Stirling Castle in Scotland | LEFT: Wikimedia Commons; RIGHT: instagram.@dr.futbal

The ball was found behind panelling in the Queen’s Chamber at Stirling Castle in Scotland | LEFT: Wikimedia Commons; RIGHT: instagram.@dr.futbal

The ball spent centuries out of sight

Stirling Castle in Scotland | Wikimedia Commons

From castle rafters to a World Cup

A leather football that dates to around 1540 has spent centuries behind the walls of Stirling Castle and was discovered during renovation work in the late 1970s. The ball was recognised by Guinness World Records as the world’s oldest football, and was found behind panelling in the Queen’s Chamber at Stirling Castle in Scotland. The chamber had been decorated in the 1540s, when Mary, Queen of Scots, was a child at the castle. The ball itself is dated to between 1540 and 1570, according to the Stirling Smith Art Gallery & Museum , which now holds it.The ball stopped at the University of Glasgow, where specialists began scanning it to produce a museum-quality digital twin, before travelling to the United States for the FIFA World Cup. The digital project uses a process called photogrammetry that combines photographs that are taken from different angles to build a detailed three-dimensional representation. University of Glasgow specialists Conor Fraser and Ben Morris captured the ball before it travelled to Miami for the Scotland-Brazil match on June 24. The university said the digital version will allow people to examine details such as its stitching and worn leather surface.The Stirling Smith describes the football as roughly the size of a small melon, and measured about 160 millimetres long, 150 millimetres wide and 140 millimetres high.It was made from thick leather panels that were stitched together and turned inside out, and inside was an inflated pig’s bladder, which provided the ball’s shape. The museum says that several repairs remain visible on its surface, which is evidence that the object was used rather than made simply for display.How it ended up behind the panelling is not known, with one possibility being that it was kicked into the roof space and became trapped there, while another is that someone deliberately put it there and forgot about it. The museum also notes the possibility that it was placed there for a symbolic purpose, although there is no evidence establishing which explanation is correct.The ball was found in a chamber that was associated with Mary, Queen of Scots, and historical records show that she took an interest in sport. But there is no evidence that she personally owned or played with this particular football, and Guinness World Records says that it is more likely that soldiers or staff at the castle used the ball for a form of handball.The football was eventually placed in the collection of the Stirling Smith Art Gallery & Museum, where it became one of the institution’s best-known objects. Guinness World Records lists it as the oldest football and dates its manufacture to the 1540–1570 period. The ball was scheduled to appear at the Coral Gables Museum in Florida from June 20 to 24 before being taken to the Scotland-Brazil World Cup match in Miami, and the University of Glasgow said it was the first time that the football had travelled to the United States.The university has been developing its “Wonder” platform through its Museums in the Metaverse programme, and used 3D models to let people examine cultural objects virtually. For a museum object that normally has to remain protected behind glass, the digital version changes how it can be viewed. A visitor does not have to travel to Stirling to see its surface at close range, and the model can be enlarged or examined from different angles without handling the original.The physical football remains at the Stirling Smith when it is not travelling, with its leather surface, old repairs and unusual construction still belonging to a fragile object that survived from the 16th century. The new scan just gives researchers and visitors another way to examine the same evidence.
Article Summary: The ball was found behind panelling in the queen’s chamber at stirling castle in scotland. The chamber had been decorated in the 1540s, when mary, queen of scots, was a child at the castle. The ball itself is dated to between 1540 and 1570, according to the stirling smith art gallery & museum.

Article Title: Minecraft Dungeons II to launch on September 29: Here's everything we know so far
Article Text:
Image credit: Mojang

Minecraft Dungeons II: Release date and platforms

Minecraft Dungeons II: A connected Minecraft world

New gear and character customisation

The Sift and the new story

Multiplayer changes in Minecraft Dungeons II

What makes the sequel different

Minecraft Dungeons II is set to launch tomorrow (September 29). Mojang is bringing its dungeon-crawling spin-off back with a new world, expanded gear systems and changes to exploration and multiplayer. The sequel follows the original Minecraft Dungeons, which launched in 2020 and attracted more than 25 million players before development ended. This time, the game moves away from its predecessor's mission-based structure and introduces a connected world players can explore on foot. It also adds jumping, new character customisation options, a new dimension called The Sift and more flexible multiplayer features.Mojang Studios and Double Eleven are developing the game, and it will be available on PC, current-generation consoles, and Nintendo’s latest systems. Here is everything players need to know about Minecraft Dungeons II before its September 29 release.Minecraft Dungeons II will launch on September 29, 2026, for PC through Steam and the Microsoft Store, Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2.There will be no PS4 or Xbox One version.The game will be available on Xbox Game Pass from day one. Xbox Play Anywhere support will also let players access compatible purchases across Xbox and PC.The Standard Edition costs $29.99, while the Deluxe Edition costs $49.99. The Deluxe Edition includes cosmetic items and the first two post-launch DLC packs.Players who pre-order before September 28 will also receive additional hero skins, a cape and a pet.One of the biggest changes is the move away from the mission-based structure of the original game. Minecraft Dungeons II introduces a connected world that players can travel through on foot instead of selecting individual missions from a central hub.Jumping has also been added for the first time. It lets players reach vertical areas, discover hidden locations, and approach combat differently. Weapons can also have unique jump attacks.The sequel retains the classless progression system but expands the ways players can customise their heroes. Armour is now divided into four pieces: head, chest, arms, and legs.Talismans provide passive bonuses, while artefacts return as active abilities. The enchantment system has also been changed, with new effects and rarities giving players more options when creating builds.Minecraft Dungeons II introduces The Sift, a new dimension created for the game. It has its own ecosystem, creatures and visual style, with inhabitants adapted to an environment that can also be dangerous for players.The story begins with the destruction of the camp from the first game, sending the heroes into a larger adventure. The Illager Council, made up of three powerful Illagers, serves as one of the threats. The game also features an environmental crisis, while side quests add detail about the world and its characters.The connected world changes as players progress, with characters needing help, areas developing, and shortcuts becoming available.Minecraft Dungeons II supports solo play and multiplayer, with built-in cross-platform support. Sessions can adjust when players join or leave, accommodating different group sizes.Players can also combine couch co-op with online multiplayer. This allows people playing together locally to join friends playing remotely. Matchmaking is available for players who want to join other groups.Minecraft Dungeons II expands the original formula without introducing character classes. Its main changes include a connected world, jumping, the Sift dimension, a larger gear system and more flexible multiplayer.Mojang Studios and Double Eleven, the teams behind the original game, are developing the sequel. It launches September 29 across current-generation consoles, PC and Nintendo’s current platforms, with Xbox Game Pass availability from day one.
Article Summary: Minecraft dungeons ii will launch on september 29, 2026, for pc through steam and the microsoft store. It will be available on current-generation consoles, pc and nintendo’s current platforms, with xbox game pass availability from day one. The standard edition costs $29.99, while the deluxe edition includes cosmetic items and the first two post-launch dlc packs.

Article Title: Nike Alphafly 4 launched with lighter ZoomX LT foam and 10% more energy return
Article Text:
Nike Alphafly 4 are 5% lighter than Alphafly 3

Two foams now sandwich the plate

The upper is designed for tired feet

Nike has launched the Alphafly 4, the newest version of its marathon racing shoe, with changes to nearly every major part. The company says it returns 10% more energy than its predecessor and weighs 5% less in a men's size 8.5.The biggest change is in the midsole. Nike has added a new ZoomX LT foam, which it says is up to 17% lighter than standard ZoomX and offers 8% more energy return. The shoe goes on early, limited sale on nike.com from today, September 17, with wider availability on nike.com and at select stores from October 29.ZoomX LT doesn't fully replace regular ZoomX. Nike layers the two foams above and below the carbon-fibre Flyplate, which keeps the Alphafly's signature propulsive scoop. The plate adds stability and guides a smooth forward roll, which should help runners hold a steady cadence. Up front, dual Air Zoom units have been retuned to work alongside the foam and plate at push-off. A lightweight Fast Shot outsole handles grip.The new Atomknit upper is seamless and breathable. It uses zoned midfoot cables, an integrated heel unit and a molded sock liner to hold the foot securely over long distances.Nike says development drew on athlete feedback across Alphafly generations, learnings from Project Dreamweaver, and extensive women's trials. Emily Farina, Senior Principal, Running Footwear, Nike Sport Research Lab, said the team studied how fatigue changes running mechanics."Our goal was simple: create a shoe that helps athletes feel more confident and capable deep into the race," she said.Nike athlete Addisu Gobena has already tested that claim. He wore the Alphafly 4 to a course-record marathon win in Sydney, and said he trusted the shoe when the race got difficult.
Article Summary: Nike alphafly 4 is the newest version of its marathon racing shoe. The company says it returns 10% more energy than its predecessor and weighs 5% less in a men's size 8.5. Nike has added a new zoomx lt foam, which it says is up to 17% lighter than standard zoomx.

Article Title: The next thing Adidas wants to make bespoke is the foam itself
Article Text:
An early prototype of Adidas's printed foam at the APEX Lab in Herzogenaurach

A foot model recreated from APEX scan data, used to build Project R.A.P. footwear

Running shoes have spent a decade getting faster through chemistry

Adidas's printed foam changes how it compresses through its structure, not a new formula

The Futurecraft 4D midsole, printed by Carbon as a lattice rather than moulded from foam. (Picture: Adidas)

Printed foam gets its behaviour from geometry

One of five printed foam versions Adidas made in three weeks.

The printed foam's underside, with openings that change in size and density from heel to toe.

Without a mould, foam can be remade for every athlete

Adidas's printed foam prototypes, which can be remade for each athlete without a mould.

Running-shoe foam has changed a great deal over the past decade, but it is still made in moulds, and a moulded midsole behaves the same way for every runner who wears that size. Adidas has been 3D-printing midsoles for close to a decade to get around that, though it has printed them from resin rather than foam.At its headquarters in Herzogenaurach, Adidas has now shown foam that comes out of a printer. It was the final stop at the APEX Lab during Home of Innovation, the company's name for a tour through the labs where athletes test products most people won't see for another year or two. Chief Creative Officer Alasdhair Willis calls it "a future continuously being built." APEX, short for Athlete Product Excellence, is the elite-only room where Adidas makes bespoke products for its biggest names.Most of the tables there dealt with how a shoe gets customised to a single athlete. One covered the profile APEX builds before anything is made: 3D body and foot scans, pressure mapping and gait analysis, the process behind boots and shoes made for Lionel Messi, Anthony Edwards, Noah Lyles and Alexander Zverev.Another held Project R.A.P., short for Radical Athlete Perception, Adidas's 3D-printed footwear platform.Its lattice boots are made from an athlete's scan data and worn in MLS matches by Philadelphia Union's Cavan Sullivan, and its basketball shoes by Brooklyn Nets rookie Mikel Brown Jr.The last table came with a warning. Mateo, the designer behind it, said the project was at a very early stage, much further from production than R.A.P., and that the group was the first outside Adidas to see it. What he showed was printed foam, in structures that could be tuned in ways a moulded midsole cannot.Foam sits under almost every athletic shoe, but running is where the race to improve it has been fought most openly. For most of the last decade, progress in running-shoe cushioning has been a materials race. EVA, the light and cheap foam that sat under most shoes for years, gave way to expanded TPU, which Adidas brought to market as Boost in 2013. The next jump came from PEBA-based foams, which are lighter and return more energy, and which now sit under most elite racing shoes.Each step came from a lab working on the formula. A better foam meant a new polymer, a new blend or a new way of expanding it. Engineers could shape a midsole, stack layers or add a carbon plate, but the foam inside a moulded midsole behaves more or less the same throughout. Changing how it compresses has meant changing what it is made of.There is a practical reason for that. Foam midsoles are moulded, and a mould can only produce shapes that can be pulled back out of it. Complex internal structures are off the table, so the chemistry has had to carry most of the load.Adidas has found a way around that limit before. In 2017 it introduced Futurecraft 4D with Carbon, a printed midsole that gets its cushioning from a lattice structure, and 2021's 4DFWD added bowtie-shaped cells coded to compress forward under vertical impact. Those midsoles are printed as an elastomeric lattice, not foam in the EVA or Boost sense, so Adidas has been able to shape cushioning through geometry for some years, though never in foam.Mateo described printed foam as a combination of two things. From additive manufacturing it takes precision, control and customisation. From foam it keeps lightness, energy return and deformation, which he called a fancy word for how squishy it is. Adidas had to develop a new additive method to make it, though Mateo didn't say what the base material is.He was wearing one of the structures, so he walked up and down beside the table to show it working. This design is meant to maximise vertical deformation, meaning how far the foam compresses under load, and it does that by collapsing forward as the runner moves. You could see the cells fold in a set direction rather than squashing evenly, as a moulded slab would.The idea of a midsole that folds forward will be familiar from 4DFWD, which produced that movement with printed resin. The structure Mateo was wearing does it in foam, with the arrangement of its cells deciding how it compresses. He said this design was only one example, and a different structure could be optimised for weight, or built for walking rather than running, from the same material. A basketball shoe has to absorb heavy landings and support sharp cuts, while a walking shoe needs comfort over hours rather than speed over minutes. If the structure decides how the foam behaves, one printed material could in principle be shaped for each of those jobs.Geometry becomes more useful once it can be adjusted for an individual. Mateo said the lab can collect an athlete's pressure data, kinematics and foot scans, and then tune the structures to that athlete. That hasn't been possible with foam before, because a moulded midsole comes out the same for everyone in a size. APEX already profiles athletes across football, basketball, tennis and running, so the data needed to shape foam for one person is being collected well beyond runners.Speed matters as much as precision. Three weeks before the session, Mateo was at the factory where the samples on the table were made, and he produced five versions of the structure, each tuned differently. The process he described was simple: make a pair, test it with the athlete in the lab, adjust it, make another pair, and narrow down to the best shoe for that athlete.Alexander Taylor, Adidas's Senior Vice President of Innovation Design & Concepts, who was leading the group, put that pace in context. With conventional manufacturing, each change means working on moulds, and the structures on Mateo's table could not be moulded in the first place. Mateo has practically been living at the factory for the past three or four months, Taylor said, because the project now moves as quickly as he can test it. The shoes also look different, since the process produces shapes nothing from a mould would.For now, the project is being judged by how the structures behave rather than by numbers. Mateo didn't share energy-return figures to compare against moulded foams, and at this stage there may not be finished ones to share.Printed foam is still a long way behind R.A.P., which already has boots on an MLS pitch. If it follows the same path, its first wearers will be the athletes whose profiles are already on file at APEX, a few steps from the table where it was shown.
Article Summary: Adidas has been 3d-printing midsoles for close to a decade to get around moulds. At its headquarters in herzogenaurach, adidas has now shown foam that comes out of a printer. It was the final stop at the apex lab during home of innovation. Adidas has been able to shape cushioning through geometry for some years, but never in foam.

Article Title: Usman Nurmagomedov reveals hidden truth about Khabib Nurmagomedov’s fight camps despite UFC retirement

Khabib Nurmagomedov leaves everything behind for fight camps

Khabib Nurmagomedov may have retired from professional MMA in 2020, but his approach to training has not changed. According to his younger cousin Usman Nurmagomedov, the UFC Hall of Famer still gives everything when he joins the team for a fight camp. Khabib reportedly spends four to six weeks fully focused on the fighters around him. He takes part in every session and demands maximum effort from everyone.Usman says there is no room for half-speed work when Khabib is around. The former UFC lightweight champion continues to play an important role in the development of fighters from his team. His intense approach has also helped shape the training culture surrounding Usman Nurmagomedov, Islam Makhachev and Umar Nurmagomedov.Usman Nurmagomedov has offered an insight into what it is like to train under Khabib Nurmagomedov during a full fight camp.Although Khabib officially walked away from professional competition in 2020, retirement has not meant stepping away from the gym. When his team begins a serious camp, he reportedly commits himself to the process for several weeks.Usman explained that Khabib can spend four to six weeks with the team during camp.He does not simply arrive for selected sessions or offer advice from the sidelines. Instead, he becomes part of the daily routine and trains alongside the fighters.“We never work at half capacity with Khabib. It’s 100 percent every time”, he said.That mindset has become a major part of the team’s training culture. Khabib expects fighters to maintain their intensity throughout each session. There is little room for coasting or taking an easy approach.The former lightweight champion retired with a perfect 29-0 professional record. He left the sport after defeating Justin Gaethje at UFC 254 in October 2020. Since then, his focus has shifted toward coaching, mentoring and supporting fighters from his team.Khabib has remained closely involved with several high-profile athletes. Islam Makhachev, Umar Nurmagomedov and Usman Nurmagomedov are among the fighters who have benefited from his guidance.Usman is currently preparing for the next stage of his own career. The 28-year-old remains undefeated and has established himself as one of the leading lightweight fighters outside the UFC. He has won titles under both Bellator and the PFL.A potential UFC move has also been a major talking point around Usman’s career. However, the fighter previously explained that contractual restrictions have prevented him from negotiating freely with other promotions.“The stars will align by the end of October,” Usman said. “Look, there’s that 90-day rule. I can’t even negotiate with anyone except the PFL. I can’t even start talking to anyone. As soon as the negotiations with PFL are over and that 90-day period expires, then we can start talking to other promotions.”Khabib’s presence is particularly important during fight camps. Rather than simply providing instructions, he is known within the team for demanding that fighters match his intensity.
Article Summary: Khabib nurmagomedov retired from professional mma in 2020. The ufc hall of famer has remained closely involved with his team. His cousin usman has revealed what it is like to train under khabib. Usman says there is no room for half-speed work when the former champion is around.

NEW DELHI: India will face Pakistan in the men’s cricket gold medal match at the Asian Games 2026 on Saturday, October 3. The much-awaited clash will be played at the Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin. The match will start at 1:30 PM local time.India booked their place in the final with a dominant 124-run win over Sri Lanka in the semi-final on Thursday. Pakistan, meanwhile, defeated Bangladesh by six wickets in their semi-final to set up a blockbuster final against India.India, led by Shreyas Iyer, were sent in to bat after Sri Lanka won the toss. They posted 169 for seven on a difficult pitch.Ishan Kishan played a key innings for India, scoring an unbeaten 80 off 46 balls. He hit four boundaries and five sixes.Teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi also made an impact on his return to the Indian XI. He scored 39 runs and helped India recover after the early dismissals of Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson.India then produced a superb bowling performance to bowl Sri Lanka out for just 45.Jasprit Bumrah struck twice in the opening over and put Sri Lanka under pressure immediately. Axar Patel, Abhishek Sharma and Washington Sundar also picked up wickets, while three Sri Lankan batters were run out.India are the defending champions in men’s cricket. They won the gold medal at the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou.Pakistan, meanwhile, will be looking for their first-ever Asian Games gold medal in men’s cricket. Their women’s team have previously won gold at the Games.The India-Pakistan final will also come after a difficult start to the men’s cricket event, with six consecutive matches abandoned because of bad weather.Pakistan entered the final after beating Bangladesh by six wickets in the other semi-final.The match was reduced to 13 overs per side because of a delay caused by wet weather. Bangladesh scored 111 for seven before Pakistan chased down the target in 11.3 overs.
Article Summary: India will face pakistan in gold medal match on saturday, october 3. India booked their place in the final with a dominant 124-run win over sri lanka. Pakistan, meanwhile, defeated bangladesh by six wickets in their semi-final. The match will start at 1:30 pm local time.
